messages:
sre-oncall: Seeing growth of apiserver 5xxs and controller-manager restarts in eu-west-1 over the last 30m. Started when a batch of GPU nodes came up. Anyone eyes on etcd?
infra-bot: [ALERT] control-plane-high-error-rate in eu-west-1 - svc: apiserver - 5xx spike - 1779129990
danielle: I pulled logs from controller-manager on cluster-gpu-03: `kube-controller-manager: panic: sync failed: timed out waiting for the server to respond` then OOMKilled a couple times.
james: ran `ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://10.2.1.5:2379 endpoint status` - leader changed 6x in 12m. `raft term` bumping often. Disk IO latency looked high on the nodes hosting etcd (nvme io wait spiking).
james: paste: ```
# etcdctl endpoint status --write-out=table
ENDPOINT          ID               VERSION  DB_SIZE  IS_LEADER  RAFT_INDEX  RAFT_TERM
10.2.1.5:2379     a1b2c3d4         3.5.1    4.3 GB   true       1254323     240
10.2.1.6:2379     e5f6g7h8         3.5.1    4.3 GB   false      1254301     239
```
marta: Scheduler queue also clogged - ~40 pods pending for GPUs. Cluster-autoscaler hit our regional quota / commitment, so it couldn't spin up new nodes. Some teams are using on-demand; that caused a burst of image pulls in the GPU pool.
will: Confirmed heavy image-pull backlog on the GPU nodes, kubelet saw overlayfs stalls: `overlayfs: writeback failed` in kernel logs. Disk saturating when IMGs pulled concurrently.
danielle: When the node disk stalls, etcd leaders on those hosts start timing out (we colocated etcd on control-plane nodes with local nvme ephemeral). Might be a structural problem for large GPU fleet boot storms.
etcd-bot: Suggestion: consider etcd leader isolation and slow disk mitigation. Leader transfer or restart may be required to stabilize cluster.
sre-oncall: Short plan: 1) cordon + drain the most IO-saturated GPU nodes (reduce image pulls) 2) force a leader transfer to a healthy etcd member off the NVMe-saturated hosts 3) scale down concurrent image-pull rate (registry rate-limit or stagger deployments) 4) open a quota request with cloud for burst capacity, or temporarily move non-sensitive jobs to another region.
james: Doing a leader transfer now: `etcdctl move-leader --to-server=10.2.1.6:2379` -> returned success but apiserver 503s persisted for a few mins while caches warmed.
marta: In parallel I've disabled autoscale bursts for the GPU-spot pool to stop adding more nodes until we verify disk behavior.
will: For immediate relief, I'm going to restart kube-apiserver on the non-leader control-plane nodes (rolling) to clear stale connections. Not ideal but reduces 503s.
danielle: FYI we should consider moving etcd to separate io-optimized volumes instead of relying on ephemeral NVMe on GPU host chassis. Cost vs reliability tradeoff for sure.
sre-oncall: Agreed. Please log cost estimate and impact: if we move etcd to provisioned iops volumes across AZs, monthly delta vs current ephemeral layout. Tagging @marta @will to follow up with infra cost.
marta: noted; opening a ticket and will draft rough numbers. Also flagging app teams to stagger scheduled batch deployments tonight. :warning:
will: monitoring dashboards: apiserver 5xx rate trending down after drains + leader move. I'll keep an eye for another leader flip.
james: putting a short postmortem stub in incidents/ after this stabilizes with timeline + remediation options.
sre-oncall: thanks everyone. If we see another leader flip we escalate to on-call infra-ops and consider temporary capacity reshuffle to another region.
